text:
Ava: Heads-up 1: SentinelBank POC tomorrow AM. They asked for a compact acceptance checklist and a short ops playbook for PrivateDeploy connectivity. Core asks: connector in their VPC, egress via their perimeter proxy, preserve client src IP, and static egress allowlist. Can someone draft? cc @Diego @Sophie
Diego: Ill take it. Quick confirm: they prefer interface endpoints (PrivateLink) for control/management plane, but legal might force peering. Include both.
Sophie: Noted. Two recommended topologies: (1) PrivateLink for control plane + onprem proxy for model egress (recommended), (2) VPC peering/TGW with routed egress (fallback).
Diego: Short firewall snippet for their network team (outbound from connector hosts):
```
# Allow outbound TLS to Redwood endpoints
ALLOW tcp 443 to management.<region>.redwood-hosted.net and models.<region>.redwood-hosted.net
# DNS (customer resolver preferred)
ALLOW udp 53 to <customer-dns-ip> or 8.8.8.8
# NTP
ALLOW udp 123 to pool.ntp.org
# If PrivateLink: allow ENI IPs for interface endpoints (we will provide list)
# If peering: allow egress to provided model IP ranges/ASNs (we will provide)
```
Sophie: Callouts to include: preserve source IP (route connector -> proxy without SNAT), stable egress IPs (we supply if requested), and SNI passthrough requirement for TLS-inspect. If they must intercept TLS, recommend mTLS between connector and proxy or cert pinning for re-signed certs.
Ava: They also asked for an operator kill-switch for egress during incidents. Can you sketch options?
Diego: Two simple patterns: (A) Manual route blackhole: operator updates route table for connector subnet to a blackhole route (immediate stop). (B) Security-group/ACL block: toggle SG or NACL rule to drop outbound to model egress. Both actions should be auditable and tied to oncall runbook.
Sophie: Add these ops tests to the runbook:
- curl health check to connector from bastion (use --resolve)
- tcpdump on proxy to confirm original client src IP
- openssl s_client -connect <proxy>:443 -servername api.redwood-hosted.net to validate SNI passthrough
- verify route table points connector subnet to proxy without NAT
ops-bot: Smoke test we recommend after allowlist applied:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-hosted.net/healthz --resolve "api.redwood-hosted.net:443:<connector-ip>"
```
Diego: Minimal acceptance checklist (one page):
- Topology chosen (PrivateLink or peering) and documented
- ENI IPs or model IP ranges whitelisted by their net team
- DNS/NTP access validated from connector subnet
- Client IP preservation validated (tcpdump sample)
- TLS handshake validated (openssl s_client)
- Smoke health check successful from bastion
- Security questionnaire bullets acknowledged
security-bot: Security bullets for questionnaire (short):
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ enforced (TLS1.3 recommended)
- Key management: Option A: customer-managed KMS (HSM) OR Option B: Redwood-managed keys with attestation report
- Audit logs: configurable export to S3/Syslog; retention options 30/90/365d
- Operator controls: RBAC + MFA for console; kill-switch actions logged & auditable
Ava: Sales note: include PrivateDeploy base + infra fee. If they want static egress IPs or reserved GPU pools, propose reserved-capacity add-on (12mo discount). Ill add numbers to the external quote.
Diego: Ill produce a 1-page checklist + 1-page ops playbook and paste here within 45m. Will include sample iptables/tcpdump snippets and a one-line kill-switch example.
Sophie: Ping me for review when posted.
Ava: Thanks team 44d
